questions.prompt: Which bug is detected by -fsanitize=undefined but NOT by AddressSanitizer?
questions.explanation: Signed overflow is arithmetic undefined behavior, which is UBSan's domain.

questions.prompt: An ASan report contains 'heap-use-after-free ... freed by thread T0 here'. What does the second stack trace tell you?
options: Where the leak will be reported
questions.explanation: The report gives the access site, the free site and the allocation site.

questions.prompt: A test compares two doubles with a tolerance written as 'if (!(fabs(a-b) > tol)) pass;'. What goes wrong when a is NaN?
options: The test crashes when it evaluates the NaN
It depends on the compiler flags only, never on the value
NaN passes the test because the comparison is false
The test fails correctly, since NaN is rejected
questions.explanation: Write fabs(a-b) <= tol: it is false for NaN, so NaN fails.

questions.prompt: Why is asserting on expected VALUES stronger than 'the program did not crash'?
options: Undefined behavior can produce wrong results without any crash
Sanitizers cannot see values, so they would miss a wrong result
Values are always faster to compute than detecting a crash
Crashes are impossible in C++, so only values can be checked
questions.explanation: In this lesson the buggy program ran to completion and printed wrong numbers.

questions.prompt: A heap buffer holds 12 doubles (96 bytes). ASan says the access is 0 bytes to the right of the region. Which zero-based index was accessed? Integer.
questions.explanation: Indices 0-11 are valid; the access is index 12.

questions.prompt: git bisect over 5000 commits: maximum number of builds? Integer.
A race makes a test fail with probability 0.01 per run. How many runs give at least 95% chance of seeing one failure? Integer.
A moving-average loop with window 3 over 8 samples is written with 'k <= w' instead of 'k < w'. At the last window, what is the largest index read? Integer (zero-based)
questions.explanation: Last window i = 8-3 = 5; k goes to 3, so index 5+3 = 8, one past the end (valid 0-7).

questions.prompt: Write three regression test cases (input and expected output) for moving_average(v, w) that would catch an off-by-one in the window loop, and state how each one fails on the buggy code.
rubric: Case such as {1,2,3,4,5}, w=2 -> {1.5,2.5,3.5,4.5}; buggy code returns 3 as the first value.
Case w=1 returns the input; buggy sums two elements per window.
Boundary case w equal to size returns one mean, or w larger than size returns empty; all with hand-computed values.

questions.prompt: Explain why ASan and TSan are run as separate CI jobs and what each protects against.
rubric: They instrument memory differently and cannot be combined in one binary.
ASan: memory errors (overflow, use after free, leaks); TSan: data races.
Mentions cost (TSan slower) and running the concurrency tests under TSan.

questions.prompt: A GDB session shows 'frame = std::unique_ptr<Frame> = {get() = 0x0}' and a segmentation fault at the line 'frame->id'. State the diagnosis and the commands you used.
rubric: Diagnosis: null unique_ptr, most likely moved from earlier.
Commands: gdb -batch -ex run -ex bt -ex 'info locals' ./prog (or run, bt, info locals interactively).
Fix idea: do not use after move, or pass by reference.
